title: Ihsan: as if you see
hookLine: to worship Allah as though you see Him, for He sees you (Hadith of Jibril, Muslim)

lines: KNEE TO KNEE, LIKE A STUDENT.
cards: Medina. A small group of companions is sitting with the Prophet ﷺ when a man walks up. His clothes are brilliantly white, his hair jet black.

There's no dust on him, no sign he's traveled, and yet nobody there knows who he is. He sits down facing the Prophet, knee to knee, and rests his hands on his thighs, like a student. And he starts asking questions.
What is Islam? What is faith? Then the third question, the one Sufis would return to again and again: tell me about ihsan.

teach.b: It's called the hadith of Jibril, and it comes at the start of Sahih Muslim's book of faith.
Asked about Islam, the Prophet names the five pillars. Asked about iman, faith, he names what Muslims believe in.
Asked about ihsan, he says: it is to worship God as though you see Him, and if you don't see Him, then truly He sees you.
When the stranger leaves, the Prophet tells them it was the angel Jibril, Gabriel, who came to teach them their religion. So the religion, in this hadith, has three floors. Islam, what you do.
Iman, what you believe. Ihsan, how you do it, from the inside. The word comes from a root meaning beauty, goodness, doing something well: ihsan is doing a thing beautifully.
The answer has two steps. The first is a high one: worship as if you could see God.
Under it is a second floor: if you can't see Him, He sees you. You're not alone in the room.
Sufis took ihsan as the name of their work, but the word belongs to every Muslim; the Qur'an says God loves the muhsinin, those who do ihsan.
And it rounds off a week that began with a sickroom: let another lead, he smiled at the rows, a choice of company, God is alive, he left the way, the heart is the house.
And now: as though you see Him.

how: Muslims learn the hadith of Jibril as a summary of the religion in three levels, islam, iman and ihsan, and prayer offered with that attention, as though seeing God, is what ihsan names.

o: believing in God's angels and books
facing Mecca five times a day
worshiping as though you see God

games.q: the hadith of Jibril — tap the pairs.
p: how you do it, from the inside

games.q: a stranger with no dust on him asks the Prophet ﷺ about ihsan. what's the answer?
o: to give generously to the poor.
to worship God as though you see Him; if not, He sees you.
games.why: as though you see Him, and if you don't see Him, He sees you. then the Prophet said it was Jibril, come to teach them.

practice: If you pray, take your next prayer with that picture: as though you see God, and if you can't, knowing He sees you; notice how your body, your pace and your attention change.
If you don't pray, choose one ordinary act, washing a cup, answering a message, and rehearse doing it beautifully, as if the one you most respect were watching.

wordCard.voice: Ihsan. Doing a thing beautifully: worshiping God as though you see Him, knowing that He sees you. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: excellence, doing beautifully; from a root meaning beauty and goodness.

carryVoice: Your line: as though you see him. And if you can't, you are still seen. That's the week.

sources.ref: Sahih Muslim 8; Sahih al-Bukhari 50 (the hadith of Jibril: islam, iman, ihsan)
